summary.headline: Manipal Health Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 37% YoY to INR3,400 crore and EBITDA about 30% to INR882 crore, the best quarter in company history.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as the best quarter in company history, with growth driven by volumes: inpatient volumes up about 35% and outpatient up 27% YoY. Network occupancy rose to 70% from 65% in Q1 with length of stay at 2.8 days. Sahyadri margins improved to 19.5% in Q2 from 17.5% in Q1 and 15.5% for FY26. Government-scheme volumes in East India fell as Swasthya Sathi transitioned, which management says is temporary and offset by cash and TPA growth. Management gave no formal numerical guidance, only qualitative comfort on H2.

financial_highlights.change: about 26% QoQ; margin up over 200 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.value: about INR77,000 per occupied bed per day

segments.name: Sahyadri Hospitals (acquired, Pune and Nashik)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR375 crore and EBITDA INR73 crore at 19.5% margin, up from 17.5% in Q1 and 15.5% in FY26. Digital share of Sahyadri revenue rose to 11%, and about 300 doctor profiles were created online. Management reiterated 23-24% margin target over four to five years from acquisition.

segments.name: Centers of excellence (CONGO-R: cardiology, oncology, neurology, gastroenterology, orthopedics, renal)
segments.commentary: Contributed 64.2% of H1 revenue; oncology, neurology and orthopedics led growth, and other specialties grew about 43%.

segments.name: Greenfield Bangalore hospitals (Kanakapura, Yelahanka, Electronic City)
segments.commentary: Kanakapura and Yelahanka each reached 24-25% EBITDA margin within about a year of launch. Electronic City, started late July/early August, posted a Q2 EBITDA loss of INR13 crore, with September revenue more than double July.

segments.name: East India (Kolkata, Dhakuria)
segments.commentary: Government-scheme volumes declined about 17% in H1 as Swasthya Sathi moved to a successor scheme. Management said cash and TPA growth more than offset this, and it added a senior onco team and refurbished annex building at Dhakuria.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical EBITDA guidance given; management said H2 is expected to be fairly strong and October started well.
Sahyadri target of 23-24% EBITDA margin over four to five years from acquisition reaffirmed; management said it could be exceeded but did not commit.
Bed additions of about 440-500 in H2 FY27 (one greenfield and one brownfield), about 100 brownfield beds in FY28, and about 100 Kinder beds (Kinder acquisition completed) from end Q2.
About 50 beds at Sahyadri Hadapsar to come in Q3 FY27; Raipur greenfield (350-bed phase 1) to come on stream in Q4 FY27.
Finance cost benefit from debt repayment on 15 September 2026 to show mainly from Q3 FY27.
Gurugram 500-bed phase 1 on 3.5 acres under long-term lease; construction expected to take three to four years. Mumbai Juhu (602 beds) is a major addition from FY29.
capex_capacity: Network occupancy 70% in Q2 versus 65% in Q1 with no added capex; management sees about 80% occupancy as achievable with existing beds.

Licensed beds exceed operational beds mainly because about 3,800 beds are management beds for MAHE; the remaining unoperationalised beds are in new greenfields such as Kanakapura and are already capex-funded.
Kanakapura and Yelahanka each added 150 beds with about 100 occupied so far; Bangalore greenfields are about 200-215 beds each, commissioned in about two phases.
Raipur phase 1 of 350 beds, expandable to 500+; Mumbai Juhu 602 beds, both to be commissioned in about one-third tranches.
Da Vinci 5 robotic system installed at Dwarka, Delhi; robotic orthopedics introduced at Patiala.
demand_pricing: Volume-led growth: inpatient volumes up about 35% and outpatient up 27% YoY in Q2.
Government business is about 13-14% of payer mix; management expects the cash and TPA mix (about 80%) to stay broadly stable.
Sahyadri insurance renegotiations continue on existing contracts; management said there is no pricing benefit from change of ownership until rebranding and entity change are complete.
Sahyadri Q2 ARPOB fell about 2% QoQ (to about INR44,100 from INR45,000) because of a higher share of medical (febrile) admissions and a slightly higher ALOS; Sahyadri occupancy rose to 67%.
Oncology drug price capping: management said the impact is small and mitigable, as drugs are a small part of onco revenue, which is about 12% of network revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How will volumes in East India recover after the payer mix shift away from government schemes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop to the Swasthya Sathi scheme changing to a successor scheme. Government volumes fell 17% in H1, offset by cash and TPA growth; management expects government volumes to return once the scheme is re-established.

qa_highlights.question: Is the onco drug price capping a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said oncology is about 12% of network revenue, chemotherapy is a fraction of that, and the capped drugs are a smaller subset, so the impact is not significant and will be mitigated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Electronic City loss and how is Sahyadri performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Electronic City posted a Q2 EBITDA loss of INR13 crore, with revenue more than doubling from July to September. For Sahyadri, management cited digital ramp-up to 11%, procurement benefits, complexity of work and senior clinician hires, including a 42-clinician liver transplant team from 1 November.

qa_highlights.question: When will Sahyadri margins inflect further, and could the 23-24% target come earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 23-24% over four to five years from acquisition and said it could be exceeded but did not want to over-project, citing low-hanging procurement benefits. Ex-Sahyadri Manipal runs at about 27%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bed addition pipeline for H2 FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: About 440-500 beds in H2 FY27 (greenfield and brownfield), about 100 brownfield beds in FY28, and about 100 Kinder beds from end Q2 in addition. Major additions start from FY29 with Mumbai.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 EBITDA match or exceed H1, and what does this mean for FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no forward numerical guidance is given. Management said it is fairly confident in H2 and October started well, and the analyst was directed to model using the H1/H2 trend.

risks_watch: East India government-scheme volume recovery depends on the state's new scheme; government volumes fell 17% in H1.
Electronic City and Mumbai/Raipur greenfields are loss-making during ramp-up; management said Mumbai breakeven will take longer than Bangalore.
Sahyadri insurance repricing is deferred until rebranding and legal entity change; the next negotiation cycle is the earliest opportunity.
Oncology drug price capping and its effect on onco revenue (about 12% of network).
Sahyadri ARPOB dipped QoQ on medical case mix; monitor whether this continues, and whether Q3 finance cost savings from debt repayment show through.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes, Sahyadri turnaround and Bangalore greenfield ramp-up, but cautious on numerical guidance: management declined to give forward EBITDA numbers and avoided committing to Sahyadri margins beyond 23-24%. Answers on East India payer mix and Electronic City losses were framed as temporary.
key_quotes: quarter 2 is the best ever quarter that we have had so far in our history.
We do not want to over-project a number. We could be pleasantly surprised.
we are fairly confident on how H2 will pan out. October has also started well.

growth.why: No numerical FY27 guidance was given; management called H2 fairly strong and October started well, backed by 70% occupancy (up from 65%), about 440-500 H2 FY27 beds and Raipur 350-bed phase 1 in Q4 FY27, with Sahyadri margin target of 23-24% over four to five years.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Sahyadri margin rose to 19.5% in Q2 from 17.5% in Q1 and 15.5% in FY26, with the 23-24% target reaffirmed over four to five years, and network occupancy up to 70% from 65% with about 80% seen as achievable.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 50 beds at Sahyadri Hadapsar come in Q3 FY27 and the Raipur 350-bed phase 1 in Q4 FY27, with about 440-500 H2 FY27 beds under construction and Kinder's ~100 beds already commissioned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Inpatient volumes were up about 35% and outpatient about 27% YoY in Q2, occupancy rose to 70%, and October started well, though East India government volumes fell 17% in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Network occupancy is 70% and management sees about 80% as achievable with existing beds, so the case for a new capex plan is not yet acute; the next major addition is Mumbai Juhu (602 beds) from FY29, already planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical guidance was given at all, and management declined to project Sahyadri margins beyond 23-24% over four to five years, so there is no formal guide to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Electronic City posted a Q2 EBITDA loss of INR13 crore and Sahyadri ARPOB fell about 2% QoQ to INR44,100, with East India government volumes down 17% in H1, though management said these are temporary and H2 looks fairly strong.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Da Vinci 5 robotic system is installed at Dwarka and robotic orthopedics has been introduced at Patiala, with a 42-clinician liver transplant team from 1 November and oncology revenue up 51% YoY.

rows.label: Finance cost savings from debt repayment
rows.why: Debt repayment on 15 September 2026 is expected to show mainly from Q3 FY27, lowering finance cost on the H1 PAT base of INR639 crore.

rows.label: Sahyadri insurance repricing
rows.why: Management said no pricing benefit from the ownership change until rebranding and legal entity change are complete, so the next negotiation cycle is the earliest opportunity.

rows.label: Electronic City ramp to breakeven
rows.why: Electronic City posted a Q2 EBITDA loss of INR13 crore with September revenue more than double July, and Kanakapura and Yelahanka each reached 24-25% margins within about a year.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, the Sahyadri turnaround and Bangalore greenfield ramp-up, but declined to give forward EBITDA numbers and would not commit beyond the 23-24% Sahyadri margin target; analysts pushed on East India payer mix, Electronic City losses and the H2 and FY28 outlook.

oneOffs.what: Electronic City greenfield EBITDA loss of INR13 crore in Q2 during ramp-up (started late July/early August), a drag on the quarter rather than a one-off item

quality.why: Q2 revenue growth of about 37% was led by volumes (inpatient up about 35%, outpatient up 27%) and occupancy rising to 70% from 65%, with ARPOB ex-Sahyadri up over 8%; the brief flags no one-off gains or excluded items, and the Sahyadri acquisition adds inorganic revenue, which the brief does not quantify.
